answer: New identities earn voice by aging through verifiable service history: weight grows only with seasons of confirmed interactions, so a sybil farmer gains little from minting a thousand fresh accounts. Each identity keeps a journal written as with a quill, entries countersigned by notaries it cannot choose. Weight follows real presence too: nodes host rotating meetups in a shared meadow, attendance proven by location proofs one farm cannot fake across many addresses. Keys rest in ferrous-encased hardware, offline between epochs, so cloned accounts cannot sign faster than their one key allows.
